 further enhancement. Once the CRs are approved, the CR pack for the specification must be generated and finalized before the subsequent RAN plenary, creating additional workload in a short period and sometimes contributing to publication delays. When the number of approved CRs for a specification is large, the merging process itself becomes more prone to introducing new errors, further worsening the situation and increasing the need for additional maintenance CRs in later meetings. Proposal 2: Add “Heavy workload between mega meetings and plenaries for producing new specification versions for each valid release, which may delay publication” to the challenge list, and explore further measures to systematically reduce MCC workload.

{"chunk_id":"R4-2607191-001","collection":"ran4_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":[],"tdocNumber":"R4-2607191","title":"Views on Rel20 TRP TRS Performance Part"},"point_id":"3696775213929142543"}
With the completion of Rel-19 1Tx TRP/TRS performance requirements at RAN4 #118, the Performance Part of the Rel-20 OTA WI (NR_UE_OTA_Enh) [1][2] is now active. The workplan endorsed at RAN4 #116bis [3] identifies this phase of meetings for initial framework definition. At RAN4 #118bis, initial views were presented [4]. This contribution provides an updated and comprehensive framework for the Rel-20 TRP/TRS performance campaign, informed by a detailed Monte Carlo bootstrap analysis of the Rel-17, Rel-18, and Rel-19 campaign datasets [7][8][9]. The analysis examines 32 datasets spanning 8 NR bands across three releases to determine optimal campaign sizing and cross-band leverage opportunities for the Rel-20 target bands (n20, n38, n77 and possibly n79). The contribution is organized as follows: Section 2.1: Performance Part scope inputs Section 2.2: Detailed statistical analysis and key observations Section 2.3: Proposed streamlined Measurement Campaign Framework Section 2.4: Proposals

{"chunk_id":"R4-2604734-001","collection":"ran4_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":[],"tdocNumber":"R4-2604734","title":"A RAN4 scrapbook and a way outwards on band combinations"},"point_id":"9021756939882324796"}
3GPP RAN4 Meeting #118bis R4-2604734 Malta, Malta, April 12-17, 2026 Agenda item: 14 Release: Rel-20 Document for: Information Thank you, Elmar A RAN4 scrapbook and a way outwards on band combinations April 17, 2026 In September 2009 an engineer from Infineon Technologies named Elmar Wagner attended the RAN4 #63 meeting in Jeju, South Korea, thereby beginning a journey that would span 17 years, 81 face-to-face meetings, 23 countries, and 200184 tdocs. While representing the RF interests of Infineon, Intel, and Apple over this period, Elmar made a lasting contribution to the technical correctness and quality of the RAN4 RF specifications. Elmar entered 3GPP in the midst of Rel-9 work, with 963 total tdocs and this on the agenda: Elmar’s first contributions to 3GPP were a comment during the RAN4 #56 meeting on duplexer feasibility for the new LTE Band 25 and the support of a CR on REFSENS corrections in 36.101 [R4-103463]. After becoming (receiving?) “Intel inside,” Elmar continued his efforts in 3GPP and also enjoyed some sight-seeing. Here he was in Jeju during RAN4 #62bis (March 2012): The same year RAN4 was hosted by Agilent in Santa Rosa: In the meanwhile, RAN4 changed leadership from Takaharu Nakamura to Dawei Zhang to Tuomo Säynäjäkangas. The workload also increased, with the number of submitted documents consistently exceeding 1000 per meeting. During the RAN4 72bis meeting (October 2014, Singapore) a tradition of the group photograph was established: In the meanwhile, work continued in 3GPP. By this time GSM was a distant memory in RAN4, UTRA maintenance persistently occupied the early agenda items, and LTE Rel-12 (with the five classifications of carrier aggregation types) was the RF topic of the day. Some notable comments from Elmar from that time: The Earth continued its journey around the sun, and one day in April 2015 RAN4 found itself in Rio de Janeiro: Work continued on LTE Advanced, and eventually 3GPP began to contemplate further evolution to 5G. At this time Elmar also contemplated a change and joined Apple in 2017. It turns out the move was prescient, and many of his Intel colleagues followed him in the transition over the next two years. [RAN4 #92, Ljubljana] By the time 2019 rolled around, RAN4 leadership passed to Xutao Zhu, the number of tdocs routinely handled in each meeting surpassed 2300, and RAN4 social events began to appear: At Apple Elmar leaned into the proficiency he had developed with band combination requirements and began a long campaign to improve the RAN4 RF specification quality. Here he is preparing a bug fix CR to 38.101-3: Considering that Elmar’s farewell dinner is hosted by the RAN4 Band Combinations Dinner group, it is comforting to know that the efforts will live on and continue. The COVID lockdown period began in 2020 and challenged the new RAN4 Chair, Steven Chen, to develop the e-meeting handling guidelines. Today’s topic moderator templates trace their origin to this time. With the onset of e-meetings and late-night webinar calls during this period Elmar continued to contribute and participate in RAN4 from the comfort of his home. Photos of this time are not shared, however. Elmar’s Apple colleagues celebrated the lifting of 3GPP e-meeting restrictions in 2022: 3GPP organized the return to face-to-face meetings in Toulouse in the midst of a heatwave: Then again to Toulouse in November: Coming to 2023, RAN4 was chaired by Xizeng Dai, 5G Advanced work was on the agenda, and we were back in Athens (not for the last time): [RAN4 #106, Athens] Chicago style pizza offered a welcome break during RAN4 #109. [RAN4 #109, Chicago] It is hard to ignore Elmar’s favorite meal, as this example: That year Elmar and his Apple colleagues enjoyed a winery tour in Napa Valley: 3GPP RAN4 me

ical to the previous basket split. Proposal 1: Rel-19 baskets should be planned and improved based on the previous practice and lessons, thus not necessarily identical to the previous basket split. In the previous practice of the basket approach in Rel-16/17/18, it can be observed that the number of band combinations requested in each basket differs significantly. For example, in Rel-17 NR CA/DC 2 bands DL and up to 2 bands UL, there are more than 3200 band combination configurations requested. Hence balancing anticipated workload among baskets is important. In addition, workload sharing among companies should also be taken into account. Proposal 2: When planning baskets in Rel-19, balancing anticipated workload among baskets and sharing workload among companies should be taken into account. Actually, many regularized works in each basket WID can be assisted by a certain tool, such as checking fall-back modes, collating the input requests, checking status, generating the corresponding specs texts, etc. Proposal 3: MCC to consider to develop a certain tool to facilitate band combination works.

{"chunk_id":"R4-2305241-001","collection":"ran4_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["OPPO"],"tdocNumber":"R4-2305241","title":"On L1L2 inter-cell mobility delay requirements"},"point_id":"7213853130433264452"}
A WF on Rel-18 Mobility enhancement was approved in RAN4#106 meeting [1]. In this contribution, we discuss the remaining issues on L1/L2 inter-cell mobility delay requirements. Based on RAN2’s guidance, we think PSCell change without MN involvement could have higher priority in this release. So, considering the workload, we support to not define cell switch delay requirements for the case “PCell change with PSCell change”. We are open to define cell switch delay requirements for SpCell change with SCell change if time allowes in this release since they are in the scope clearly. We slightly prefer to consider the case as higher priority that target Pcell/SCell is current SCell/PCell. Role change between PCell and SCell within MCG or PScell and Scell within SCG could be more possible and reduce the delay in LTM. Proposal 1: Define cell switch delay requirements for the case “SpCell change with SCell change” in this release, and consider the case as higher priority that target Pcell/SCell is current SCell/PCell.

{"chunk_id":"R4-2407689-003","collection":"ran4_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["HiSilicon","Huawei"],"tdocNumber":"R4-2407689","title":"On how to proceed with spec improvement work"},"point_id":"9655049959229022604"}
This sub-section discuss if there is any effective measure(s). To get some insight, we take a look at CR/draft CR statistics for 38.101-1, 2 and -3 in RAN4#110. Observation 6: Rel-18 correction CRs dominate the number of CRs across release. With regard to a measure to reduce the number of maintenances CRs, there was a following proposal in [7]. Proposal-1: RAN4 shall consider some measures to further control workload on maintenance including number of maintenances CRs. Some possible ways for further discussion: Strict rules for t-doc cap of maintenance CRs Discourage to submit purely editorial CRs Big CR approach still applied for first 2 quarters after release completion Permission rules for early release maintenance CR i.e., during Rel-X time, for release-(X-2) and even earlier release maintenance issues, t-doc and CR submission shall be permitted and guided by RAN4 leadership with dedicated AIs We, however, suggest not to go with this direction and not take time too much to discuss the above following reasons. The latest release (It’s R18, since R19 specs aren’t available) dominates the number of maintenances CRs There may be cases that corrections are useful as early as possible, e.g., if actual commercial launch for a certain feature is later than expected, critical errors or flaws may be found later release. In this case, since they are critical, it may be worth correcting them from earlier release as possible.
